summary: State fire tower near Ashford, built 1936 with CCC labor; 1965 40-ft R-6 replacement removed or destroyed in 1969; footings and debris remain on a gated state-land road.

facts.design: 1936: 60-ft wooden tower with 8x8 cab (CCC). 1965: 40-ft wooden DNR tower with R-6 live-in cab
facts.status_note: Lookout gone; the 1965 replacement tower was removed or destroyed in 1969. Sources describe footings and debris; the original cab's whereabouts are unknown

access.note: Hike is on state land; the road is probably gated at the start of its 4 miles, and visitors are asked not to block gates. No closure described

visit.trail_note: About 4 miles of road walk if gated, with 1,100 feet of gain; route from Highway 706 east of Elbe, past the Nisqually River

events.note: 60-ft wooden tower with 8x8 cab, built by the CCC
Aircraft Warning Service post activated August 14, 1942 (Seattle Filter Center); manned 24 hours a day during WWII

40-ft wooden DNR tower with R-6 live-in cab replaced the 60-ft tower. Forest Lookouts also gives 1964-66 from a state biennial report

1965 tower removed (register) or destroyed (firelookout.com, Willhite) in 1969

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's R-6 design and 12.2 m (40 ft) describe the 1965 replacement. The original 1936 tower was 60 feet (about 18.3 m). The story gives both.
Register and Willhite give 1965; the Forest Lookouts page also gives a 1964-66 range from a state biennial report. The story reports both.
Register says the 1965 tower was removed in 1969; firelookout.com and Willhite say destroyed. The story reports the disagreement.

notes_for_editor: The record's R-6 design and 12.2 m height describe the 1965 replacement, not the 1936 original (60 ft). Editor may want the height labelled. Willhite's route starts near Elbe and Ashford, which the page does not place in a county; the Forest Lookouts page says north central Lewis County. Willhite says the cab was placed at Camp Six but could not find it today; no source says whether the cab survives. The garage's fate after 1943 is not in the sources. Used 1 web search and 5 page reads.
